page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment ("thodi,", the end of "Methodi") and is kept as a fragment. The small cup-shaped marks (⌣) after "Aristotelis", "corruscatione" and "percipere" are printed signs, probably references or quantity marks, and are copied as they appear; their meaning is not clear from the scan. "plerag;" is an abbreviation (plerasque) whose last letters are doubtful. The page is set in roman with italics. The paragraph runs on from the previous page and ends mid-word at "succin-", which continues on the next page.
